text:
alex: heads-up — p95 latency doubled for the us-east inference pool around 10:20 UTC, customers seeing timeouts. looks correlated with a collapse in prefix cache hit-rate on shard g-3 :eyes:

maria: link to graphs? can you paste the hit-rate numbers?

alex: dashboards->https://our-grafana/board/kv?orgId=1&var-shard=g-3
alex: kv.prefix_hit_rate: 0.91 -> 0.08 between 10:17-10:21, evictions/sec spiked from ~120 -> 12k

sameer: saw the spike in eviction churn on nodes in that pool. tail of key-cardinality exploded for a few noisy tenants. suspect prefix key explosion + aggressive pruning kicked in.

jen: any recent deploys or config flips?

deploy-bot: rollout finished: service/eng-runtime:v2026.3.18-1100 to us-east-1 at 10:16 UTC

kai: hmm the rollout included the kernel-selection fallback tweak (PR #4219) to prefer compatibility on some model shapes. note: that change toggles `kernel.selection.fallback` to true during warmup.

alex: copying relevant config diff:

```
- kernel.selection.strategy: "latency_prefer"
+ kernel.selection.strategy: "compat_fallback"
+ kernel.selection.fallback: true
```

sameer: profiling trace from one node shows a lot of calls routed to `generic_attention` instead of `cuda_fast` and KV lookup times ballooning. sample from perf:

```
kernel=generic_attention latency_ms=11.8 count=14231
kernel=cuda_fast latency_ms=2.9 count=761
kv.lookup_ms avg=0.72 -> 5.1
```

maria: so kernel fallback is slower and increases per-request CPU/KV pressure, causing prefix cache evictions because requests keep introducing new prefixes?

jen: also noticed `kv.prefix_prune_ratio` was lowered in the same deploy to make cache more aggressive about trimming. that combo could be lethal.
jen: diff for cache flags:

```
- kv.prefix_prune_ratio: 0.25
+ kv.prefix_prune_ratio: 0.10
```

alex: ok action plan: 1) flip kernel.selection.fallback=false on us-east canary 2) bump prefix_prune_ratio back to 0.25 3) throttle top noisy tenant if still noisy

maria: i'll flip the kernel flag now on canary host group via /admin/flags

maria: `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control/flags -d '{"kernel.selection.fallback":false}'`

maria: flag flip applied to canary (g-3-a). observing...

sameer: while that's rolling, i'll prepare a hotfix to revert the prune ratio change and stage it for canary too.

deploy-bot: flag change: kernel.selection.fallback=false applied to group g-3-a at 10:26 UTC

alex: canary metrics look promising — prefix hit-rate jumped from 8% -> 77% on g-3-a within 30s, p95 down ~40%

kai: looks consistent with kernel perf improvement reducing KV pressure. move to flip on remainder of us-east if stable for 5m.

maria: rolling flag to rest of us-east now.

jen: prune ratio revert queued and applying to canary in 2m.

sameer: also enabling a temporary rate-limit on noisy tenant t-451 to reduce cardinality injection.
sameer: `rbacctl throttle tenant t-451 rate=50rps`

alex: nice. timeline so far: deploy at 10:16 triggered two related changes (kernel fallback + prune ratio). those combined with a noisy tenant burst caused eviction storm -> hit-rate collapse -> latency spike.

maria: post-mortem next steps:
- revert risky config in prod by default
- add a canary gating check for kv.hit_rate after kernel selection flips
- instrument kernel fallback path to emit `kv_pressure` metric
- playbook: automated rollback if prefix_hit_rate drops >20% within 5m of flag change

kai: will file follow-up PRs for the metrics and gating.

deploy-bot: rollout of kernel flag to all us-east nodes completed at 10:34 UTC

alex: metrics after full flip: prefix_hit_rate avg = 0.89, p95 latency back to normal, evictions/sec down to ~140.

jen: leaving the prune-ratio revert on a 10m canary then promote.

sameer: thanks all — we'll keep the noisy-tenant throttle until we confirm stable for 6h.

alex: great work. please add notes to the incident doc and tag infra-oncall for postmortem.
